items.title: Add support for constraints in `uv add`
items.reason: Canonical issue for using a constraints file with `uv add` to seed `uv.lock` without persisting those constraints in project metadata.

items.title: Add support for `-c` constraints in `uv add`
items.reason: Implemented the required capability and tested that constraints guide locked versions without being recorded as project requirements.

items.title: uv pip install don't change pyproject.toml and uv.lock. How can i sync this
items.reason: Closely matches the reported pip-install/freeze workaround; maintainers recommend using `uv add` directly because pip-interface commands do not update project metadata or `uv.lock`.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using literal terms for `uv add`, constraints, `uv lock`, `pip freeze`, requirements import, and multi-step resolution; conceptual terms for retaining locked versions, dependency preferences, minimal changes, and transitive upgrades; and fix-oriented searches for historical constraints support. astral-sh/uv#16508 and astral-sh/uv#12490 were excluded because they concern persistent or sync-time external constraints. astral-sh/uv#14011 concerns isolated build dependencies, while astral-sh/uv#8585 concerns automated minimum-version bumps.

type_reason: The report asks how to perform a workflow that current uv behavior already supports. No incorrect behavior or missing functionality is established: one-time constraints can guide the first `uv add`, and compatible versions from the existing lockfile are preferred during the second add.
summary: astral-sh/uv#11986 and merged astral-sh/uv#12209 establish the required `uv add -c` workflow; astral-sh/uv#15020 confirms that the pip-install/freeze round trip should be replaced with direct project commands.
draft_response:
Yes. You can do this directly with the project interface:

```console
$ uv init
$ uv add package_a==1.0.2 -c package_a_constraints-1-0-2.txt
$ uv add package_b==1.3.0
```

`uv add -c` applies the constraints to that resolution without persisting them to `pyproject.toml`. The selected versions are written to `uv.lock`. During the second command, uv prefers compatible locked versions, so `package_c==1.5.0` should remain selected, while `package_d==2.0.5` must move to `2.1.0` to satisfy `package_b`. This workflow was added in astral-sh/uv#11986 and implemented by astral-sh/uv#12209.

If `package_d>=2.0.0<3.0.0` is literal metadata, add the missing comma: `package_d>=2.0.0,<3.0.0`.
